heading: IMPLEMENTATION OF THE PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN
CHAPTER I
translated_text:
CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Purworejo Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous Region.
3. Regent is the Regent of Purworejo.
4. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and the Regional House of Representatives in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the Region.
5. Technical Regional Apparatus is a Regional Apparatus that administers government affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection.
6. Village is a village and customary village or called by another name, hereinafter referred to as Village, is a legal community unit that has territorial boundaries authorized to regulate and manage government affairs, the interests of the local community based on community initiative, rights of origin, and or traditional rights that are recognized and respected in the government system of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia and located in Purworejo Regency.
7. Village Government is the Village Head or called by another name who is assisted by village apparatus as an element of Village Government administration.
8. Sub-district is part of the territory of the District as a District apparatus.
9. Female Victim is a woman who experiences suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, economically, socially, and other losses caused by violence, exploitation and/or gender-based discrimination whether occurring in the public sphere or in the sphere of personal life.
10. Child Victim is a person who is not yet 18 (eighteen) years old including a child still in the womb who experiences suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, economically, socially, and other losses caused by violence, exploitation and/or discrimination whether occurring in the public sphere or in the sphere of personal life.
11. Protection of Women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.
12. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
13. Discrimination is any restriction, harassment or exclusion either direct or indirect based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that result in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and basic freedoms in life both individual and collective in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life.
14. Violence is any act of abuse of physical force with or without the use of means, unlawfully and causing misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of liberty unlawfully.
15. Exploitation is an act with or without the consent of the victim which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or Services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial.
16. Child Maltreatment is all forms of violence against children committed by those who should be responsible and/or those who have power over the child, who should be trusted namely parents, close family, teachers, supervisors, law enforcement officers, caregivers and companions.
17. Prevention is all efforts to prevent Discrimination, Violence, and Exploitation, as well as recurrence of occurrences against Women and Children.
18. Service is all efforts and actions to fulfill the rights of Female Victims and Child Victims of Discrimination, Violence, Exploitation, Child Maltreatment, and neglect which includes complaint Services, health, social rehabilitation, legal assistance and enforcement, repatriation, social reintegration, and restitution.
19. Assistance is all efforts and actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for self-empowerment of Female Victims and Child Victims of Discrimination, Violence, Exploitation, Child Maltreatment, and neglect of Women and Children to resolve the problems faced so as to provide a sense of security and comfort and have readiness and/or ability to obtain Services and live their lives.
20. Assistant is a person or group or organization that is trusted and/or has the skills and knowledge to assist Female Victims and Child Victims of Discrimination, Violence, and Exploitation with the aim that Female Victims and Child Victims feel safe and comfortable in accessing Services.
21. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA is a Regional technical implementation unit established by the Regional Government in providing services for Female Victims and Child Victims of Discrimination, Violence, Exploitation, Maltreatment, neglect and other problems.
22. Forum for the Protection of Violence Victims hereinafter abbreviated as FPKK is a coordination forum for Prevention, handling and empowerment of Female Victims and Child Victims of Violence and other problems whose implementation is carried out in a networked manner and established at the Regional, District, and Village levels.
23. Integrated Service Center is a non-structural institution that coordinates the implementation of an integrated Service system for Female Victims and Child Victims.
24. Social Reintegration is all efforts to strengthen the readiness and ability of Female Victims and Child Victims to regain their welfare in social, political, economic, and cultural life with dignity, including strengthening acceptance and support into the family and/or community environment for the protection and fulfillment of the rights of Female Victims and Child Victims.
25. Restitution is compensation payment given to Female Victims, Child Victims and/or the victim's family by the perpetrator based on a court decision that has permanent legal force for material and/or immaterial losses suffered by Female Victims, Child Victims and/or the victim's family.
26. Legal Aid Provider is a legal aid institution or community organization that provides legal aid services based on laws and regulations.
27. Business World is a commercial organization, the entire industrial and goods/services production environment, including State-Owned Enterprises, and Regional-Owned Enterprises as well as private or entrepreneurs and their networks, who will carry out their social responsibilities.

heading: Article 17
translated_text:
Article 17

1. The Regional Government provides comprehensive protection to women from various acts of:
a. threats;
b. Discrimination;
c. Violence; and
d. Exploitation.
2. Every form of threatening act as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a conducted either verbally or non-verbally that is intentionally directed at women so as to make them feel threatened in life or safety is prohibited for any reason whatsoever.
3. Every form of Discrimination act as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b conducted leading to gender, racial, or equality injustice so as to degrade the status, freedom and opportunities of women is prohibited for any reason whatsoever.
4. Every form of Violence act as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c conducted either physically, psychologically, or sexual violence so as to cause trauma to women is prohibited for any reason whatsoever.
5. Every form of Exploitation act as referred to in paragraph (1) letter d conducted in any form that degrades the dignity, worth, and honor of women and causes harm to women is prohibited for any reason whatsoever.

heading: Article 18
translated_text:
Article 18

The Regional Government provides protection to women by:
a. establishing social security;
b. building women-friendly follow-up referral services; and
c. providing supporting facilities and infrastructure for the protection of women.

heading: Paragraph 1

heading: Article 19
translated_text:
Article 19

1. Social security as referred to in Article 18 letter a is conducted by the Regional Government together with the Village/Sub-District Government, the Business Sector, and the community.
2. Social security as referred to in paragraph (1), is conducted by:
a. reporting if there is information of the occurrence of acts of threats of Discrimination, Violence, and/or Exploitation against women;
b. implementing protection of Women Victims of acts of threats of Discrimination, Violence, and/or Exploitation;
c. conducting Assistance and empowerment of Women Victims of acts of threats, Discrimination, Violence, and/or Exploitation; and/or
d. conducting security measures against perpetrators of Discrimination, Violence, and/or Exploitation against Women who have the potential to endanger life safety.

Article 24

2. Recipients of reports as referred to in Article 23 paragraph (3) shall protect both the reporter and the victim.

Article 25

1. Physical and psychological health for Women Victims of Discrimination, Violence, and/or Exploitation is intended to reduce and treat physical and psychological trauma.
2. FKPP shall facilitate or provide Assistance or treatment for Women Victims of Discrimination, Violence, and/or Exploitation.

heading: Article 26
translated_text:
Article 26

1. Women Victims of Discrimination, Violence, Exploitation, maltreatment, and/or neglect who experience trauma shall undergo a gradual rehabilitation process physically, psychologically, and socially.
2. Rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by the Regional Government through the Technical Regional Apparatus and may involve related Regional Apparatus and/or the community to assist in accelerating the rehabilitation process.
3. The Regional Government shall guarantee the fulfillment of the living needs of Women Victims of Discrimination, Violence, Exploitation, maltreatment, and/or neglect during the rehabilitation process.

heading: Article 27
translated_text:
Article 27

1. The provision of Restitution shall be carried out in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
2. The amount of Restitution paid by the perpetrator to Women Victims of Discrimination, Violence, Exploitation, maltreatment, and/or neglect or their heirs shall be based on:a. the results of mediation agreement; and/orb. court decision.
3. The Regional Government through related Regional Apparatus shall oversee the Restitution payment process to ensure it is appropriate and on target.

heading: Article 29
translated_text:
Article 29

1. The Regional Government shall provide active and comprehensive protection to children from various acts of:
a. threats;
b. Violence;
c. Exploitation;
d. neglect;
e. Child Maltreatment; and
f. Injustice.
2. Every form of threatening act as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a, whether verbal or nonverbal, deliberately directed at children so as to make them feel threatened in life or safety, is prohibited for any reason.
3. Every form of violent act as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b, whether physical, psychological, or sexual violence, that causes trauma to the child is prohibited for any reason.
4. Every form of exploitative act as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c, carried out in any form and not in accordance with the child's developmental age according to general views, laws and regulations or local wisdom and causing harm to the child, is prohibited for any reason.
5. Every form of neglectful act as referred to in paragraph (1) letter d that neglects the responsibility as a parent, guardian, or foster parent toward the child is prohibited for any reason.
6. Every form of maltreatment as referred to in paragraph (1) letter e, carried out by exploiting closeness or abuse of responsibility toward the child so as to cause physical or psychological trauma or is deemed contrary to laws and regulations, is prohibited for any reason.
7. Every form of unjust act as referred to in paragraph (1) letter f, carried out by parents toward children that discriminates or shows favoritism as well as injustice in equality between males and females.

heading: Article 30
translated_text:
Article 30

Forms of protection provided by the Regional Government as referred to in Article 29 include:
a. reduction of vulnerability risks;
b. establishing social safeguards; and/or
c. provision of facilities and infrastructure supporting child protection.

a. reporting if there is information on Violence, Exploitation, neglect and/or Child Maltreatment;
b. protection of child witnesses and Child Victims by separating them from perpetrators in temporary care facilities;
c. Assistance to Child Victims; and
d. securing perpetrators of violence who potentially endanger life safety.

Article 37

1. Physical and psychological health for Child Victims of Violence, Exploitation, Child Maltreatment, and/or neglect aims to reduce and treat physical and psychological trauma.
2. FKPP facilitates checking and treatment of physical and psychological health for Child Victims of Violence, Exploitation, Child Maltreatment, and/or neglect.
3. FKPP facilitates the conduct of visum et repertum and visum et psikiatrikum on Child Victims of Violence, Exploitation, Child Maltreatment, and/or neglect for investigation purposes.

heading: Article 38
translated_text:
Article 38

1. Child Victims of acts of Violence, Exploitation, Child Maltreatment, and/or neglect who experience trauma undergo rehabilitation in stages both physically, psychologically, and socially.
2. Rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out by the Regional Government through the Technical Regional Apparatus and may involve related Regional Apparatus and/or the community to assist in accelerating the rehabilitation process.
3. The Regional Government guarantees the living needs of Child Victims as referred to in paragraph (1) during the rehabilitation process.
4. During the rehabilitation process, provision of food intake, education, play world, and appreciation for children experiencing trauma as referred to in paragraph (1) is adjusted to age and developmental needs.

translated_text:
Article 39

1. Provision of Restitution is in accordance with laws and regulations.
2. The amount of Restitution paid by the perpetrator to Child Victims of Violence, Exploitation, Child Maltreatment, and/or neglect through parents, guardians, or the Regional Government is based on:a. results of mediation agreement; and/orb. court decision.
3. The Regional Government through related Regional Apparatus oversees the Restitution payment process so that it is used for the needs of Child Victims of Violence, Exploitation, Child Maltreatment, and/or neglect.

heading: CHAPTER XII
translated_text:
CHAPTER XII

Article 50

2. Internal supervision of the Regional Government is carried out by the Regional Apparatus that has the duties and functions of supervising the organization of regional government.

The community has the right to provide aspirations in the form of ideas and suggestions to the Regent for the improvement of Services and facilities for the organization of protection of women and children.

heading: CHAPTER XIII
translated_text:
CHAPTER XIII

AWARDS

Article 52

1. The Regional Government grants awards to individuals, families, groups, Business World, non-governmental organizations, and/or other institutions that have contributions and important roles in efforts to protect women and children.
2. Awards as referred to in paragraph (1) may be in the form of:
a. money;
b. business tools or equipment; and/or
c. certificates and certificates.
3. Further provisions regarding the requirements and procedures for granting awards as referred to in paragraph (1) are regulated in a Regent Regulation.

heading: CHAPTER XIV
translated_text:

Article 53

The Technical Regional Apparatus serves as coordinator in the organization of protection of women and children.

heading: CHAPTER XV
translated_text:

Article 54

1. Funding for the implementation of protection of women and children is sourced from the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget.
2. In addition to the funding source as referred to in paragraph (1), the implementation of protection of women and children may be sourced from:a. Village Revenue and Expenditure Budget; and/or b. other legitimate and non-binding sources of income.

heading: CHAPTER XVI
translated_text:
CHAPTER XVI

1. In the event of changes to the nomenclature, duties, functions, and authority of Regional Apparatus, the responsibilities as regulated in this Regional Regulation shall automatically remain binding by adjusting proportionally to its duties and functions.
2. In the event of unclear division of duties, functions, and authority as referred to in paragraph (1), the Regent shall appoint the Regional Apparatus most appropriate to carry out such obligation or responsibility.

heading: ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF PURWOREJO REGENCY
translated_text:
ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF PURWOREJO REGENCY

NUMBER 13 OF 2022 CONCERNING IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

heading: I. GENERAL
heading_path: ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF PURWOREJO REGENCY
translated_text:
I. GENERAL

Constitutionally, the purpose of the state is none other than to protect the entire nation, advance general welfare, and educate the life of the nation. This is clearly stated in the preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. The phrase protecting the entire nation contains a philosophical as well as moral dimension, where the state without discrimination must be able to be a protector of all its people. This commitment must be realized in various regulations and policies made by the state, so that it is no longer something that can be negotiated.

As is known, the position of women and children is very vulnerable to various kinds of violations including violations of their human rights. Strategic steps need to be taken supported by policies, such as socializing the importance of protection and at the same time fulfilling their rights both in the family, society and at every level of education. The rights and protection of women and children are basically also mandated in the 1945 Constitution, so it has become the duty and responsibility of the state to protect them. The presence of the state in this context can be realized not only by the central government, but also by Regional Governments.

Regional Governments as representatives of the state have the most strategic position in implementing the protection of women and children. To be able to realize this, Regional Governments need to have a legal basis to be able to encourage various policies that provide protection for women and children. Here, the idea to be realized is to encourage Regional Governments to create programs or policies that are women-friendly and child-appropriate. The purpose is none other than how later in community life, the world of education, and the business world become parts that are mutually synergistic to realize the implementation of protection of women and children.

The Regional Government of Purworejo Regency needs to anticipate the emergence of complex problems that occur in fulfilling protection for women and children. Policies implemented must be able to provide a sense of security and comfort for women and children. In addition, policies for implementing protection of women and children must be followed by efforts to strengthen the involvement of Regional Governments, Village Governments, the Business World, educational institutions and the community. With this responsibility, it will be able to build a Society that cares for, respects, and values women and children. Efforts to empower and protect women and children in the Region require a legal umbrella that functions as a guide and direction for all parties. For this reason, based on the authority possessed by the Regional House of Representatives and the Regional Government, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation concerning the Implementation of Protection of Women and Children.

heading: Article 2

translated_text:
Article 2

Letter a
What is meant by "the principle of humanity" is providing protection and respect for human rights, dignity, and the dignity of every Indonesian citizen and specifically women and children.

Letter b
What is meant by "the principle of respect and fulfillment of the rights of women and children" is a series of actions to respect, appreciate and ensure the fulfillment of the rights of women and children.

Letter c
What is meant by "the principle of non-discrimination and non-exploitation" is respecting equality of degree without distinguishing, both parties, on the basis of race, ethnicity, nationality, skin color, social status, affiliation or ideology and so on, as well as respecting the position and honor of women and children without any utilization that is contrary to the values that exist in society.

Letter d
What is meant by "the principle of harmony" is a view to live harmoniously and in balance that encourages a state of peaceful, calm, and happy relations between individuals.

Letter e
What is meant by "the principle of protection" is the provision of protection to create tranquility in society.

Letter f
What is meant by "the principle of justice and gender equality" is encouraging a balance between rights and obligations in accordance with laws and regulations. Letter g What is meant by "the principle of welfare" is the fulfillment of material and non-material needs.

Letter g
What is meant by "the principle of proportionality" is placing something according to proportion by looking at the situation, condition, place and time while prioritizing a balance between rights and obligations.
